feature_sets._note: A == B == C == D for this pipeline because no endpoint identifier, capture identifier or target-derived column is in the feature matrix to begin with. Endpoint identity enters only through graph structure, so the endpoint-masked condition is realised by an evaluation protocol (endpoint-disjoint splitting) rather than by dropping a column, and the scenario-masked condition likewise.

duplicates.note: Repeated flow records are a genuine property of scan and brute-force traffic and are NOT removed. They are reported so that the contribution of memorisation can be bounded, and protocol B groups them so that no duplicate straddles a split.

endpoint_predictiveness_multiclass.interpretation: Flow-weighted mean purity is an upper bound on the accuracy of a detector that sees only the endpoint identity and predicts the majority class of that endpoint group. A value near 1 means the label is almost determined by identity, so any model given the endpoint pair can reach that accuracy without learning anything about traffic.

node_feature_divergence_train_only_vs_al.interpretation: Non-zero divergence confirms the train-only aggregation is actually doing something: if it were zero, the 'train only' setting would be cosmetic.

A.residual_transductive_element: The node INDEX spans all splits, so a node that appears only in test exists in the graph during training. It carries all-zero behavioural features and no training edge, so no test traffic and no test label reaches the model through it; what leaks is the bare existence of an address. Under leave-one-endpoint-out this is the held-out device. An inductive variant that rebuilds the index from training endpoints alone is the stricter alternative and is listed in the recommendations.
